articles.title_orig: Israel’s election yielded a stalemate. Which means Netanyahu won
articles.title_zh: Israel’s election yielded a stalemate. Which means Netanyahu won
articles.content_orig:
Record voter turnout and early exit polls leave neither major political bloc with a clear path to a governing majority. Fox News Digital’s Efrat Lachter reports from Tel Aviv, Israel.
TEL AVIV, Israel — Updated Israeli exit polls early Wednesday showed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu gaining ground against his political rivals but still falling short of a parliamentary majority, leaving the country facing a possible political deadlock despite a combined majority of seats projected for parties outside his governing bloc.
An updated Channel 12 exit poll at 3:30 a.m. (Israel time) projected 53 seats for Netanyahu's right-wing and religious bloc, compared with 49 for the main opposition led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot and another 19 for Arab parties. Together, the opposition and Arab factions would hold 68 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, although they remain divided over forming a government together.
Netanyahu struck a defiant tone in his first election-night speech at Likud headquarters in Jerusalem, declaring that his party had emerged as the largest in Israel and calling for the formation of a strong right-wing government.
FORMER ISRAELI ARMY CHIEF GADI EISENKOT EMERGES AS NETANYAHU’S LEADING ELECTION CHALLENGER
"We are still waiting for the actual results, which we will receive over the next day or two," Netanyahu told supporters. "Two things have become clear. The first is unequivocal: Likud is the largest party in Israel."
"We must establish a strong national right-wing government," he added, warning against a government dependent on Arab parties, which he accused of opposing Israel's existence.
His remarks came hours after Eisenkot took the stage at his campaign headquarters in Tel Aviv, where supporters celebrated earlier projections showing the opposition ahead. Eisenkot called on Netanyahu to accept the results and step aside, but the updated numbers underscored how uncertain the race remains. Netanyahu also said Israel faced a "once-in-a-lifetime historic opportunity" with Trump to eliminate the existential threat from Iran.
A polling station in Herzliya, Israel, on Oct. 27, 2026, as Israelis head to the polls in the country's first national election since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas massacre. (Efrat Lachter for Fox News Digital.)
The competing speeches highlighted the central question emerging from the election: Who will be given the first opportunity to form a government? If Eisenkot can secure recommendations from at least 61 lawmakers, potentially including Arab parties, he could receive the first mandate despite Netanyahu's Likud emerging as the largest individual party. But that would not guarantee he could assemble a governing coalition. For Netanyahu, the election remains a waiting game. Even without a majority, he could still be tasked with forming a government — or get another opportunity if Eisenkot's efforts fail — leaving Israel facing weeks of political negotiations.
Israelis turned out in exceptionally high numbers Tuesday for the country’s first national election since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas massacre, with initial exit polls showing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud emerging as the largest party but his governing coalition falling short of a parliamentary majority, potentially opening the door to a change in leadership.
A supporter of former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, reacts to the exit poll at his party headquarters, on the evening of Israel's national election, in Tel Aviv, Israel Oct. 27, 2026. (Shir Torem/Reuters)
FORMER ISRAELI PM EMERGES AS WILD CARD IN HIGH-STAKES ELECTION WITH MIDDLE EAST'S FUTURE AT STAKE
The results are preliminary projections, not an official vote count, and could change as ballots are tallied in the coming days.
The election followed an extraordinary day at polling stations across Israel, with long lines and voter participation reaching levels not seen in decades.
Israeli voter turnout surged to a historic high, with 77.7% of eligible voters casting their ballots by the time the polls closed, according to Israel's Central Elections Committee. The figure marked the highest turnout recorded since 1999, underscoring the intensity of the country's national election.
The unusually high participation prompted election officials to streamline voting procedures and assure voters that anyone arriving at a polling station before the 10 p.m. deadline would be allowed to cast a ballot.
The vote was widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu's leadership following three years of war and continuing questions about responsibility for the security failures that allowed Hamas terrorists to kill approximately 1,200 people and abduct 251 others on Oct. 7, 2023.
JD VANCE DECLINES TO ENDORSE NETANYAHU DESPITE TRUMP'S STRONG BACKING
Residents of Jerusalem cast their votes on Oct. 27, 2026. (Yoav Dudkevitch/TPS-IL)
Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, campaigned on his record of confronting Iran and its regional proxies , highlighting Israel's military achievements and his relationship with President Donald Trump . His opponents accused him of failing to accept responsibility for the October 7 security failures and opposed his government's approach to investigating the failures that preceded the massacre.
Throughout the final hours of the campaign, Netanyahu, Eisenkot , former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett and other party leaders mounted an intensive effort to mobilize supporters and win over undecided voters.
Netanyahu's Likud party prepared hundreds of targeted campaign videos and social media messages, making digital outreach a central part of its last-minute election strategy.
Eisenkot's campaign pushed supporters to rally behind Yashar as the leading alternative to Likud, while Bennett traveled between cities and engaged voters directly and through WhatsApp conversations.
The key question now is which candidate can secure the support of at least 61 lawmakers when President Isaac Herzog consults with the newly elected parliamentary factions. If Eisenkot can obtain those recommendations, including from Arab parties, he would have a strong claim to receive the first opportunity to form a government, even though Netanyahu’s Likud is projected to remain the largest individual party. Crucially, Arab parties could recommend Eisenkot without formally joining his governing coalition. However, the final decision rests with Herzog, who is tasked with selecting the lawmaker he believes has the best chance of forming a government. Securing the first mandate would not guarantee Eisenkot could assemble a governing majority, leaving the possibility of another political deadlock.
NETANYAHU FIGHTS FOR POLITICAL FUTURE AS ISRAEL HEADS TO POLLS WITH IRAN THREAT LOOMING
Former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot attends an event for his Yashar party, ahead of Israel's national election in Tel Aviv, Israel, October 25, 2026. (Ronen Zvulun/Reuters)
The campaign's closing hours also featured personal appeals, phone calls to undecided voters and aggressive turnout operations across the political spectrum.
The final days were particularly important because a relatively small share of voters remained undecided about which party to support.
A Times of Israel poll published five days before the election found that 87% of respondents had already made their final choice, while 2.4% remained undecided between the pro and anti-Netanyahu political blocs.
Other surveys suggested a larger pool of undecided voters, although many were choosing between parties within the same political camp rather than switching sides.
That distinction could prove decisive in Israel's parliamentary system, where political parties need at least 3.25% of valid votes to enter the 120-seat Knesset.
Even a slight change in the vote share of smaller parties could shift several parliamentary seats and determine whether either camp has a realistic path to power.

articles.content_orig:
It’s Warhammer Day on Saturday, and it’s not just about celebrating our own miniatures – there are also sales and reveals for a world of video games, merch, and more on the cards.

The delightfully devious stealth platformer Deathmaster has its story trailer revealed today. The story centers around Vinheek, a powerless Skaven prisoner when we first meet him, who has plans for greatness. Vihneek is freed by Skiteek, a fellow assassin from Clan Skrell – but Vihneek’s savior is ultimately his new captor. Clan Skrell wields Vihneek as a weapon, forcing him to complete deadly contracts at all costs and with no mercy. Every target Vihneek kills propels him higher within the Clan Skrell’s ranks, but looming threats from rival clans swirl…
Deathmaster is coming to Steam , XBOX Series S|X, PlayStation 5, and Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027, so get your knives sharpened and prepare to claw your way to the top of the Eshin hierarchy.
Battlesector turns 5 this year and to celebrate, a free update is landing on Warhammer Day adding a new map, gameplay options, and a major rebalance of units across the game. XBOX Play Anywhere also goes live today.
The next big DLC, Courage and Catastrophe, is also coming on 14 December , adding a 13-mission story campaign and three new units into the oodles of content already available.
Loads more updates and announcements are happening across our licensed merch partners and video game partners, so we’re going to have a quick-fire dash through them.
Wētā Workshop are hard at work on the next stunningly detailed 1:10 scale Warhammer statue, and have prepared a little teaser. Can you guess who it is? You will have to wait until later this year to find out for sure.
The Warhammer 40,000 Character Encyclopedia by DK Books has been expanded, adding even more characters so you can learn about the movers and shakers in the 41st Millennium. Check out these new page spreads. You can pre- order now !
Displate has revealed metal posters featuring key art of the four factions from Dawn of War IV . Not only that, but they have also revealed Warhammer 40,000 Shards are coming soon. Shards are mini metal prints with three rarity levels, built for collecting. Keep an eye on Displate for more information.
If you’ve ever wanted to enjoy Warhammer Art at an even bigger scale then now is the time to do so. Triptych is a new three piece wall art format available from Warhammer Art, beginning with this stunning Armageddon artwork.
We’re just over a week away from the launch of Warhammer Survivors on 10 November , which gives us just enough time to tell you about two new characters who’ll be selling you weapons and artefacts in-game.
Lord-Magnate Brokk Grungsson flexes his mercantile ways in the Mortal Realms, while Technoarchaeologist Daedalosus helps uncover lost artefacts in the 41st Millennium.
Also, you can prepare for the release by checking out a range of new Warhammer Survivors gear from the Warhammer Merch Store !
Staying with the Warhammer Merch Store – give praise to the Dark Gods with a new Chaos banner (coming soon, subject to final approval). Plus, a profane offering of additions to a wide swathe of clothing and accessories including Dawn of War IV desk mats on top of the Survivors gear available from today.
Check out two new entrants from the next line of TOMY plushes – the Blood Angels Intercessor and an adorable Nurgling wearing its tongue as a scarf. They’re hitting shelves in 2027, along with more as-yet-unrevealed designs.
Collect new artefacts from the legendary First Founding Chapters courtesy of Starforged , who revealed a line of magnetic Space Marine helmets today displaying their unique iconography and modifications.
You may have noticed that Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 is out now – go and give it a try! Developers Auroch Digital have announced today that a Nintendo Switch 2 version will be released on 19 November .
Discover classic artwork appearing on Warhammer Combat Cards from now until 6 November before they revert to their usual miniature appearances.  You can also use the code WARHAMMERDAY in-game to get a bounty of free cards, plasma, and coins.*
Fresh from decking out Warhammer fans in clothing from the Empire of Man, Warhammer Armoury turns its attention to the lands of Bretonnia with a first preview of their latest costume set. For the Lady!
Cubicle 7 Games is celebrating the launch of its all-new Fifth Edition of Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay ! The classic RPG turns 40 this year. You can pre-order the core rulebook now, and you'll get a free PDF copy to play immediately.
Danilo have revealed their new Warhammer 40,000 Calendar.
Load up on Warhammer merch and games across the Warhammer Day celebration with a wide assortment of sales and promotions:

articles.content_orig:
The Unesco-listed region is home to cone-shaped rock formations known as ‘fairy chimneys’, created by ancient volcanic activity
Three people, including a foreign national, were killed on Thursday when a rock spire collapsed in Turkey’s Unesco-listed Cappadocia region after a landslide triggered by heavy rain, officials said.
The region, a magnet for tourists from around the world, is home to cone-shaped rock formations known as “fairy chimneys”, created by ancient volcanic activity.
“According to initial findings, two people were killed and five others injured in the incident,” Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said on social media.

articles.title_orig: 'Wolverine-style claws' discovered in carry-on bag at Seattle airport security: TSA - ABC News
articles.title_zh: 'Wolverine-style claws' discovered in carry-on bag at Seattle airport security: TSA - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
The passenger voluntarily abandoned the claws at checkpoint.
Two Transportation Security Administration officers discovered a dangerous bladed item that came straight out of an X-Men comic inside a carry-on bag during a security check at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport.
TSA officer Douglas Linn found the bladed claw, that the agency described as "a mix between Wolverine-style claws and Freddy Krueger blades", while the unidentified passenger's carry-on was going through the X-ray machine in August.
"I saw three blades and distinct claw-like features," Linn said in a statement released this week. "I was amazed, and even more so when it came out of the bag. I have never seen anything like this during my two years at TSA."
TSA Officer Dennis Oishi searched the bag and safely removed the bladed claws, according to the agency.
Oishi asked the passenger if there was anything sharp in his bag and the passenger allegedly said no at first but then "immediately remembered the items after Oishi removed them from the bag," according to the TSA.
The passenger voluntarily abandoned the claws at the checkpoint, the TSA said.

articles.title_orig: Von der Leyen touts ‘associate member’ status for Canada over objections of EU capitals
articles.title_zh: Von der Leyen touts ‘associate member’ status for Canada over objections of EU capitals
articles.content_orig:
Watered-down version of statement to be issued at end of Montreal summit instead offers ‘ever closer association’
The EU has backed away from its offer to Canada to start talks on becoming an “associate member” after disagreements between member states just as an EU-Canada summit was set to begin in Montreal.
A draft of a joint statement to be issued after the end of the summit, which runs Thursday and Friday, showed a watered-down version offering “an ever closer association of Canada to the EU, short of full membership itself”.
The issue was triggered after the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen , surprised nearly everyone by announcing in last month’s state of the union address that the EU would consider “associate membership” for Canada.
The declaration had been hailed as a landmark in EU history, offering a non-EU country such close ties to the bloc, which has not allowed any state membership since Croatia joined in 2013.
It was also seen as a sign that the call by Canada’s prime minister, Mark Carney , at the Davos summit in January for “middle powers” to work together was paying off.
But instead of announcing a work programme on developing “associate membership”, the draft communique, seen by the Guardian, states the two sides would “work to define by the 2027 EU-Canada summit the concept of an ever closer association of Canada to the EU, short of full membership itself, to reflect, through this even closer association, our common endeavour and cooperation towards our shared goals of prosperity, economic security and strategic autonomy”.
Associate membership had been mooted, and rejected, previously for countries such as Ukraine.
Von der Leyen’s declaration caught EU capitals by surprise and led to pushback politically and legally. Given “associate status” has no definition, diplomats wondered about such issues as whether Canada could join the European Council, legislative bodies or decision-making processes without a vote.
At a meeting on Monday, ambassadors in the EU raised concerns about the dramatic offer, but vowed to make efforts to seek a diplomatic path to rescinding the offer of “associate” membership without embarrassing Von der Leyen. It is understood that Italy suggested “associate membership as proposed by the commission”, with the definition to be thrashed out later by member states.
Germany walked back further, suggesting the wording “an ever closer association of Canada” to the EU.
“Nobody was consulted about associate membership apart from [Von der Leyen’s] closest staff, it would seem. Many member states, including Germany, were not happy. This is all about fixing the plane while it is flying,” said one diplomat.
Germany had argued that “associate membership” should be reserved as an interim step for prospective candidate countries, such as Ukraine or Montenegro, noting that the status has no formal grounding in current EU treaties.
Donald Trump, the US president, previously called the EU’s proposal to make Canada an associate member “laughable”, and said if he ​interpreted the move as a “hostile act” the US might stop trading with Europe “on many things”.
A bitter trade war with the US, a longtime ally, has seen Carney seek out new trading partnerships around the world. Ahead of the summit in Montreal, one of Canada’s largest banks released a report suggesting there was “meaningful” upside for Canada if it were to deepen economic ties with Europe. Tens of billions of dollars in additional trade would be possible if barriers were removed in areas of overlapping interest such as defence, energy, critical minerals and digital markets, TD Economics said .
Carney has spoken specifically about the need to lessen reliance on Elon Musk‘s Starlink satellite network, following a decision to throttle its usage over Ukraine.
Earlier this week, Carney posted on social media that Canada would join the popular music competition Eurovision. But despite fears raised by political rivals, Carney has said Canada has no interest in formally joining the EU. Changing Canadian laws to bring it in line with European nations would probably prove unpopular, despite public support for stronger ties.
Carney told reporters on Tuesday that the summit this week was the launch of further formal negotiations that will take place another year.
“The good news is it doesn’t matter about ⁠specific names or nomenclature,” Carney said. “What matters is the difference it will ​make to the lives ​of Canadians.”
A previous draft statement ​had included at least two references to Canada as an “associate member”, ​including an acknowledgment that ‌defining the ​term would take ​another year.

articles.title_orig: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17bn deal it says will expand customer options
articles.title_zh: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17bn deal it says will expand customer options
articles.content_orig:
DoorDash said Thursday that it will buy Instacart for $17 billion, uniting one of the nation's top grocery delivery services with a major food delivery company.
DoorDash, which will pay $65 per share for Instacart, said the acquisition will benefit communities by enabling more supermarkets to use Instacart's platform to run their websites.
"Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day," Tony Xu, co-founder and CEO of DoorDash, said in a statement. "Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery."
Consumers will benefit by having more stores to choose from, speedier delivery options and access to savings when they shop locally, DoorDash also said in announcing the acquisition.
"Instacart customers could shop at more than 50,000 additional stores, on top of the nearly 100,000 stores on the Instacart platform today," DoorDash said.
Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada.
DoorDash was founded a year later in San Francisco as a restaurant-delivery business and expanded into grocery delivery in 2020 amid a pandemic-induced surge in demand. The San Francisco-based company later teamed with the supermarket chain Kroger in 2022 and with Costco last month.
The deal will beef up DoorDash's grocery delivery services, making it a more potent competitor to Amazon and Walmart.
DoorDash's most recent earnings report , released on Wednesday, shows its revenue grew 34% from a year ago. Its total number of orders rose 28%, a sign the company is continuing to grow in the highly competitive delivery business. By the end of 2024, DoorDash held nearly 61% of the food delivery market share, topping Uber Eats and Grubhub, which held around 26% and 6%, respectively, according to Consumer Edge .
The acquisition is the latest sign of consolidation in the delivery services industry, which is increasingly dominated by larger players. As competition intensifies, companies like Instacart have struggled to maintain their market share. Instacart now commands 18% of spending on U.S. delivery platforms, down from 26% five years ago, according to Consumer Edge, a market research company.
DoorDash's acquisition of Instacart  also comes as more people migrate from in-person stores toward apps to order their weekly groceries. Nearly 150 million Americans grocery shopped online as of 2025, according to Capital One .
As online shopping becomes more prevalent, some companies are experimenting with personalized pricing, which involves using AI and consumer data to charge shoppers different prices for the same item.
The advocacy group Groundwork Collaborative has slammed the practice as unfair and predatory. In a months-long investigation last year, the group found that identical grocery items on Instacart could differ in price by as much as 23% from one customer to the next.
Federal regulators are now scrutinizing such practices. The Federal Trade Commission on Thursday said it has opened a probe into DoorDash and Instacart, along with seven other companies across retail and transportation, to examine how they set prices.
DoorDash, which has a market value of $73 billion, said the companies will operate as separate entities until the merger is finalized, which is expected in late 2027 or early 2028. After the deal closes, DoorDash said it plans to maintain Instacart's brand, technology and app.
The Associated  Press contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Iran’s hidden web of military agencies is slipping hardware past the US blockade
articles.title_zh: Iran’s hidden web of military agencies is slipping hardware past the US blockade
articles.content_orig:
An investigation by Reuters has unveiled an extensive military and financial network in Iran, comprising over 5,000 entities. This network is reportedly used by Tehran to import equipment and components critical for manufacturing missiles and drones, bypassing Western sanctions and the American naval blockade.
Records reviewed by the agency reveal that a single entity within this network imported equipment and materials valued at $2.3 billion between January 2025 and June 2026, covering a period that includes the first four months of the war that erupted in February of the same year.
The imports included materials for rocket fuel production, explosives, aircraft engine components, electronics, and heavy-duty trucks that could be used as mobile launch platforms. Shipments reached Iran by land, sea, and air, even during the conflict.
The investigation relied on thousands of banking and government records, company registration documents, and import data, in collaboration with Israeli-American risk consultancy firm, 240 Analytics.
According to the documents, entities within the network begin with the letters 'WDJA', an acronym for the Iranian Ministry of Defense, followed by numbers identifying each entity. All are registered with a single address in Tehran, the location of the Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics.
These entities list February 11, 1979, as their founding date, but records indicate most were actually established around 2013, coinciding with tightening sanctions, declining oil exports, and the currency collapse.
Some entities have connections with the Revolutionary Guard and semi-governmental economic institutions known as 'bonyads,' controlled by members of the Iranian elite.
Noam Benstock, chief analyst at 240 Analytics, described the numbered entities as the “invisible infrastructure” that facilitates sanction evasion.
Unique government identification numbers have allowed tracking of their transactions via bank accounts, invoices, and shipping bills, even when operating through front companies.
Despite sanctions on Iranian military institutions, Reuters found no evidence that the numbered entities reviewed were explicitly listed on Western sanction lists.
Purchases Without Cross-Border Transfers
According to the investigation, the network relies on intermediaries and front companies abroad, using revenue from sanctioned Iranian oil sales to purchase and ship goods to Iran.
Import data showed that 97% of the shipments reviewed were recorded as settlements “without money transfer.” Instead of cross-border fund transfers, intermediaries bought equipment using balances in foreign banks.
Bank records revealed that 36 entities within the network had foreign currency deposits worth $1.2 billion by the end of 2024, while the local currency reserves for the rest of the network amounted to approximately $1.8 billion.
Former U.S. Treasury official Meyad Maleki described the system as the regime's “military lifeline,” enabling Iran to convert foreign oil sale revenues into military purchases.
The entity 'WDJA 346428' emerged as a key importer in the network. According to records from the trade data platform Import Genius, its imports amounted to $2.3 billion from January 2025 to June 2026.
Purchases included chemicals for missile fuel and explosives, along with precision machinery suitable for manufacturing missile and drone structures and components.
Peter Salisbury, a researcher on Iranian arms transfers and adjunct assistant professor at Columbia University, suggested that the data indicates a broad effort to rebuild or expand Iran's arsenal, showcasing the procurement system's adaptability in finding new routes.
Experts in weaponry and sanctions who reviewed the investigation's findings confirmed that many materials could serve military programs, while noting that some have dual uses for civilian purposes as well.
Reuters clarified that some import records lacked detailed descriptions, necessitating reliance on customs codes to identify contents and declared origins without independent verification in all cases.
The investigation also utilized documents published by the website 'Wiki Iran'. Reuters noted it could not identify the site's operators, though the site confirmed the authenticity of its materials and sources through connections within and outside Iran.
Based on import data and shipping documents, equipment entered Iran via ships across the Caspian Sea from Russia, trucks from Central Asia, and cargo planes from China.
Data showed that monthly import value decreased by 47% to $54 million in March, compared to the previous month, before rising to $77 million by May.
Documents also registered imports from Germany and other EU countries, including trucks and aircraft engine components and electronics.
The network's purchases included hundreds of trucks from 'Iveco' and thousands of 'Toyota Hilux' and 'Land Cruiser' models, according to reviewed records.
In response to Reuters' inquiries, 'Iveco' stated it had contractual guarantees to prevent its products from reaching prohibited entities or military use, though it lacks control over products carried by third parties with no direct contractual relation.
The company confirmed its trucks' presence in Iran occurred beyond its control and responsibility.
'Toyota' asserted it does not conduct business in Iran, was not involved in the purchases mentioned in the investigation, and is unaware of them.
The Chinese Foreign Ministry claimed no knowledge of the incidents presented and rejected attempts to associate China with regional hostilities.
A European Union spokesperson stated that member states are responsible for enforcing the bloc's sanctions and continue to evaluate information regarding Iran's missile and drone program enhancements.
Several Iranian governmental and company entities contacted by Reuters, including the Iranian presidency and Tehran's UN mission in Geneva, did not respond to detailed requests for comment, nor did the Russian Defense Ministry, U.S. Treasury Department, White House, or U.S. Central Command.

articles.title_orig: Finland launches criminal investigation into Google’s clearing of forest for datacentre site
articles.title_zh: Finland launches criminal investigation into Google’s clearing of forest for datacentre site
articles.content_orig:
Google has called Finland its home for over 15 years, but its most recent move in data-center expansion in the country has brought some unwanted neighbors for nearby villages. Wolves have descended upon Finnish villages in Muhos and Otanmaki following Google’s illegal felling of hundreds of thousands of trees to prepare for a multibillion-euro data-center expansion—prompting a stop order from Finnish authorities.
“We had wolves coming into the village because all the wild animals moved out of the forest,” Anni Ranta, a resident of Otanmaki, told The Guardian . “They fled.”
Google’s Finnish subsidiary, Tuike Finland Oy, cleared an estimated 330 hectares—or 815 acres—of forest near Finnish town Muhos and almost 200 hectares—or about 494 acres—near Otanmaki, before completing required environmental assessments. The clearings involved an estimated 400,000 trees across the two locations according to The Guardian .
Finnish authorities ordered the tech giant to suspend all preparatory work at both sites while environmental assessments are completed. The Finnish Licensing and Supervision Authority ordered Google to halt preparatory activities at Muhos and the Otanmaki site near Kajaani. The authority said the work included removing trees and topsoil, constructing access roads and making other changes that could significantly alter the environment before the required assessments had been completed.
“In our opinion, the measures in question will change the environment and cause impacts, the identification and assessment of which are among the key objectives of the EIA procedure,” Tommi Muilu, Head of the Environmental Department at the Finnish Licensing and Supervision Authority, said in a press release .
Google posits it acted in “good faith” and did not intend to cause environmental harm outside of Finland’s statutes. The company also announced plans to plant trees across 130 hectares at Muhos. The planned replanting covers less than half the area cleared at Muhos alone.
“We understand the concerns and have fallen short of our own high standards in this instance,” a Google spokesperson told CNBC . ““We acted in good faith under the Forestry Act, and ran nature surveys and put in place measures to protect high-value areas. As we continue our long-term work in the region, we are advancing our landscaping and biodiversity plans, which include tree planting across 130 hectares at Muhos.”
The clearances are part of Google’s planned €13 billion (about $15.1 billion) investment in Finland, announced in September. The company intends to expand its data center infrastructure across the country as demand grows for cloud computing, digital services and AI workloads.
“Google is supporting clean energy projects, and dedicated nature and community funds to support local biodiversity, education, research, and workforce development,” Google’s press release read.
Google did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Fortune .
Finland has become an attractive destination for data center developers because of its cool climate, access to low-carbon electricity and availability of land. Cooler temperatures can reduce the energy required to cool servers while the country’s electricity mix includes nuclear, wind and hydropower.
Google has operated data centers in Finland for years. Its existing Hamina facility has been operational since 2011, using seawater from the Gulf of Finland in its cooling system—a design the tech giant has touted as an alternative to conventional cooling approaches. The facility also draws on Finland’s electricity infrastructure.
And Finland went out of its way to land Google’s $15.1 billion project. “Finland is an attractive destination for investments, and attracting further investment remains a top priority,” Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said in Google’s announcement in September. “Google’s decision is a clear testament to our strengths.”
The Nordic country welcomed the tech giant with open arms. Google partnered with Fingrid—Finland’s national electricity transmission system operator—and Business Finland—Finland’s official government organization and public funding agency—to identify locations for the company’s infrastructure. In September, it also signed a 22-year deal with Fortum to help extend the life of the Loviisa nuclear plant, which Google says supplies about 10% of Finland’s electricity.
“Without the lifetime extension investment program, the plant–which currently employs approximately 580 people and provides 10% of Finland’s electricity–could not continue operations beyond 2030,” Google said in a press release . “Keeping this clean energy asset online for decades to come will help stabilize electricity prices and support long-term resilience of Finland’s grid.”
But according to the European Commission, data centers are a growing environmental and climate challenge due to their large consumption of electricity and water needs. Their carbon footprint also depends on whether the electricity powering them comes from low-carbon or fossil-fuel sources.
“Sustainable, flexible and well-designed data centres that can adjust their electricity use to the grid conditions, can help lower the overall cost of the electricity system, improve grid stability, and integrate more renewable energy,” the Commission wrote.

articles.title_orig: Fairy chimney rockfall kills two at Turkey's Cappadocia tourist attraction after heavy rain
articles.title_zh: Fairy chimney rockfall kills two at Turkey's Cappadocia tourist attraction after heavy rain
articles.content_orig:
Parts of a large volcanic rock formation crashed down in Turkey’s popular tourism destination of Cappadocia on Thursday, killing at least three people and injuring five others, officials said.
A section of the rock formation — known as a fairy chimney — tumbled in Cappadocia’s Goreme region, prompting authorities to deploy medical and rescue teams.
Gov. Huseyin Kok said recent heavy rains likely caused the collapse, which occurred near a parking lot at an entrance to the site.
He said rescue teams were continuing to search for other people who may be trapped under the debris.
“We hope that there are no other casualties,” the governor said. “We are deeply saddened.”
Kok said two of the three dead were Turkish nationals. He did not provide information on the third victim.
Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said an investigation was launched into the incident.
HaberTurk news channel showed heavy machinery removing chunks of rock from the foot of the formation.
Cappadocia, in central Turkey, is a UNESCO World Heritage-listed site famed for its distinctive rock formations and ancient underground cities. It is one of the country’s most visited tourism locations.
The collapse occurred on Turkey’s Republic Day holiday, when the area would have been crowded with visitors.

articles.content_orig:
On his 368th day without a job, Dia Harris woke at 8:30, slipped a coffee pod into his Keurig and checked his iPad to see how many more rejections had come in overnight.
There were two automated messages from “Meta Careers,” thanking him for applying to be a program manager. “Our recruiting team will contact you if your qualifications are a strong match,” Harris read. By his count, those were the 560th and 561st roles he’d sought since getting fired from the federal government.

articles.title_orig: Zwift Plus Explained: Zwift Video Routes & Zwift Coach Hands-On
articles.title_zh: Zwift Plus Explained: Zwift Video Routes & Zwift Coach Hands-On
articles.content_orig:
If you buy through our links, we may earn an affiliate commission. This supports our mission to get more people active and outside. Learn about Outside Online's affiliate link policy
(Photo: Zwift/Corie Spruill)
Video routes mean more routes Lots of new badges to chase Quality machine learning based structured training system Workouts use group rides and RoboPacers instead of just ERG mode Immediate post-ride coach analysis on pacing and fatigue
Requires an upgraded Zwift Plus premium subscription When deviating from the plan feedback is unclear
Today, Zwift is launching Zwift Plus. This new premium tier pushes the monthly cost to $29.99, with a discounted yearly option at $299.99. In exchange for the upcharge, you unlock two core upgrades: real-world video routes and adaptive coaching.
Zwift considers this a massive milestone, which is why I recently went to Moab to celebrate the video-based routes ahead of launch. The concept was to ride the route indoors, then ride it outdoors to see how perfectly they matched. Unfortunately, we caught the tail end of a Pacific hurricane, so I only got to drive the route and ride it inside. Still, the big reveal ended up feeling almost anti-climactic—but in the best way possible.
The inside perfectly matches the real world, but you still get all the Zwift details you are used to. Zwift lays the graphics seamlessly into high-resolution and high frame rate footage. I rode the Tron bike in Arches National Park, and while it sadly doesn’t glow on the road, the wheels sit perfectly on the video road and the speed adjusts as you ride without ever breaking the illusion. It’s underwhelming, but only because it’s really good and feels like a natural extension of what Zwift already does. If you’ve used Rouvy, which Zwift now owns, this is better.
Personally, though, I don’t find the video-based routes all that much of a draw. They provide more variety, and that’s great, but Zwift already adds routes all the time and anyone who’s used Zwift knows the team is great at recreating real-life locations. What this launch is really all about is coaching, and that’s where the real magic is.
Part of why the team at Zwift considered this launch such a high-stakes proposition is that it’s a price increase, and that always comes with baggage. You could even consider the addition of the video routes to the Zwift Plus plan as a sort of tiered pricing structure where, all of a sudden, you have to pay for more routes. That’s not really true, but I can understand the hesitation.
I think part of why I don’t see that as an issue is because I don’t find the video routes to be the major news here. They are additional content, and as someone who will likely chew through every single additional badge Zwift offers this winter, that’s nice, but also not a big deal. Instead, I see this as a pretty clear value proposition of $10 a month for structured training.
With that in mind, my favorite thing about Zwift Plus is that I see it as a product that is going to consolidate the structured training market. I believe this will be a big hit to TrainerRoad, and I think that for many people, Zwift Plus will represent a net decrease in monthly subscriptions.
The reasons for this are pretty simple: structured training has to be good enough, and it has to create an environment where the user actually follows the plan. Before this launch, Zwift was mostly failing at both of those requirements.
Zwift already had training plans; they just weren’t engaging, they weren’t reactive, and they were widely considered to be not that great. With Zwift Plus, the first correction was the quality of the plans, and to address that, Zwift brought on Ryan Cooper.
If you aren’t familiar with the name, Ryan Cooper is the founder of Best Bike Split and the former Chief Scientist at TrainingPeaks. To understand why his involvement is so important, you have to look at what Best Bike Split actually does. It is a predictive physics engine that takes a rider’s specific power profile, weight, and aerodynamics, layers it over the exact elevation of a race course, and calculates exactly how many watts that rider should push on every single segment to finish as fast as possible without blowing up.
That is the level of data-driven modeling he brings to Zwift, and it is exactly why the brand is very careful to call this new coaching system “machine learning” rather than “AI.” Right now, AI is a marketing buzzword. When most people hear it, they picture a chatbot scraping the internet and hallucinating a generic training plan based on a text prompt.
Machine learning is different. It relies on math and datasets. In this case, Cooper’s algorithms were trained on the anonymized power and heart rate data of millions of Zwift riders, combined with peer-reviewed sports science. The system isn’t guessing or estimating based on what it read online. It uses actual machine learning to recognize patterns in your specific history, power data, and daily fatigue, and then mathematically calculates exactly what you need to do today to actually get faster.
This means Zwift has now solved the quality problem that TrainerRoad has so far always held as an advantage. But the raw quality of workouts is actually somewhat secondary in real life. You need not only quality workouts, but you need workouts that people will complete, and this is where Zwift has something no one else does.
Zwift controls everything about where you ride your bike, and that means the Zwift Plus workout plan has options. Once you set up your plan, the system will recommend an ever-changing variety in terms of how you complete a workout. My favorite example was actually the first day of the 12-week plan I started, when I was scheduled for a route rather than a set of intervals.
Except, if you squinted a bit, you’d see a clear interval workout. The route was the Watopia Mountain Route, and while it might appear to be a free ride, the route starts with a few miles of flats, then it climbs for a while before descending and finishing with some flats. What is actually happening there is that you get about 8-10 minutes of warm-up, then you have a work block of about 40 minutes before you get a rest, and finally a 20-ish minute cool-down where you ride the flats again. And Zwift knows, based on all your past rides both inside and out, exactly how hard you will ride each of those sections. Except I actually went harder because I started late and wanted to finish faster, so in my case, I got a notice asking if I wanted to adjust my plan based on the new intensity.
In the first week, I also had traditional intervals and a follow-the-RoboPacer session. The result is a tight training plan that adapts to you if you don’t follow it exactly, but rarely looks like a tight training plan. It’s a sort of trick to keep you engaged, and my money is on it working very well.
The only problem with this system is that, at launch, there’s not enough AI and there’s not enough feedback. I am told some of this will come, but it’s not super clear when or how much, so I have to evaluate what exists right now—and right now, it needs more interaction.
I am sure many people will not want to hear that this should have a chatbot, but I think it should. It has to be a good one, but for more than a year now I’ve bounced around between different AI systems, and when it works, it’s incredibly helpful. For a long time, I used Google Gemini paired with Garmin Connect, and this summer I’ve been playing with RideWithDave. Whatever system I’ve used, the main benefit is that you can ask the robot about deviations. “I have this scheduled; what if I do this instead? Does that fulfill the same goal?” Or, the opposite happens plenty, too: “Hey, I had this scheduled but instead I did this; did I satisfy the goal?” With the Zwift system, you just have to guess.
And once you do guess, there’s very little feedback one way or the other. One day, I had an interval session scheduled that was 2×20

articles.content_orig:
🎮 The Zelda 40th anniversary Switch 2 is out today, October 29, but Walmart and Target are planning online restocks for November 6
🚨 Our Zelda Switch 2 restock tracker @mattswider on X will send out an alert as soon as stock appears
👀 Walmart was our top pick to have a restock, but a supply chain delay has pushed the date back
⌚ GameStop, Best Buy, and Nintendo are holding in-store midnight launches where units will be available
Update (11:23 AM ET): Nintendo announced a restock at the Nintendo Store , though it seems to be flashing in and out of stock. We were able to add it our basket after a few tries.
Walmart: Zelda Switch 2 console
Best Buy: Zelda Switch 2 console
GameStop: Zelda Switch 2 console
Target: Zelda Switch 2 console
Nintendo: Zelda Switch 2 console
🚨 We’re tracking Zelda Switch 2 stock updates. If you’d like to know when more stock arrives, follow Matt Swider on X and turn on notifications. You can also become a free or paid subscriber to The Shortcut to help support our work. 🚨
A new update has dashed our hopes of a major Walmart restock of the Zelda Switch 2 console, which we were confident would happen today. However, a new Reddit post (thanks, Wario64 ) has revealed that Walmart is waiting until at least November 6 to sell the special edition console online.
🚨 Want the Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2? Drop your email for restock alerts before it sells out. ⤵️
A employee note says: “Due to a supply chain delay, some stores may not receive the Nintendo Switch 2 Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition in time for its planned Oct. 29 release. To allow time to fulfill preorders and reshop inventory as needed, the point-of-sale (POS) block will remain in place through at least Friday, Nov. 6. As inventory arrives, orders will be fulfilled based on preorder priority and available inventory.”
The Redditor who posted the news shared that some people were able to get the console from Walmart after 8:00am local time, so there is still hope.
Target recently updated its Zelda Switch 2 listing to reveal that it will also start taking orders of on November 6, with in stores orders beginning November 5. Clearly, the supply chain delay is impacting other stores, otherwise we likely would have seen a restock take place today, as we initially predicted.
We now know that Walmart and Target will be taking online orders, and that Best Buy and Nintendo are holding in-store events on November 5. GameStop is also letting customers pre-order in-store via their website .
Despite the news, we’ll still be tracking every retailer with our restock tracker, which provides up-to-the-second information whether something is in stock. If the Zelda Switch 2 does appear – which it might – our followers will still be one of the first to know.
Up next: PS5 Pro restock: it’s available again, but you’re paying more than you should

Formerly TechRadar’s Gaming Hardware Editor, Adam has also worked at Nintendo of Europe as a Content Marketing Editor, where he helped launch the Nintendo Switch. He also runs a retro gaming YouTube channel called Game on, boy! Follow him on X @ItsMrProducts .

articles.title_orig: Serious pollution by water industry remains high despite £5bn investment, say regulators
articles.title_zh: Serious pollution by water industry remains high despite £5bn investment, say regulators
articles.content_orig:
South West Water has been given the lowest possible environmental rating by the Environment Agency over high levels of pollution.
The regulator downgraded the firm from two stars out of a possible four to one, meaning it is now considered a "poor performing company" for its environmental impact.
It said it had performed "significantly below target" for sewage pollution incidents for the 15th year in a row.
South West Water, which has 1.8 million customers across Devon, Cornwall, the Isles of Scilly and parts of Dorset and Somerset, said it knew there was "much more to do" and was taking action to improve areas that "matter most" to customers and the environment.
The annual Environmental Performance Assessment grades England's nine water and sewerage companies largely on how often they pollute rivers, streams and the sea.
For 2025, South West Water was among four companies rated as poor performing, or one star, while four others were rated as requiring improvement, two stars.
South West Water performed "significantly below target" for sewage pollution incidents [BBC]
Severn Trent Water was the only company to achieve the highest rating of four stars.
The Environment Agency's report card comes a month after South West Water was fined almost £8m for a series of pollution-related offences over six years.
In the last year it also recorded the sharpest rise in customer complaints of any water company .
Serious incidents in the past year include pollution in St Austell River , killing thousands of fish, while pollution at Exmouth meant beachgoers had to leave the water .
Industry regulator Ofwat said the company met seven of its 23 targets in 2025-26, with below target performance for "most areas".
It noted its performance in relation to water supply interruptions "deteriorated substantially" and, despite improving annual performance by 38%, said the company's total pollution incidents performance remained more than double its target.
Customer satisfaction also remained challenging, ranking 15 out of 17 in the sector.
While storm overflows performance improved by 19%, it still fell short of its target, the Environment Agency said.
It was, however, the only company to have met its target for internal sewer flooding, or how often wastewater enters a property, every year since 2020-21.
A spokesperson for South West Water said: "We are under new management with a renewed focus on improving our performance.
"We know there's much more to do and although it will take time, we are taking action and making progress in the areas that matter most to our customers and the environment."
They said the firm had "reduced spills from storm overflows by 17% last year alone, with spill duration down by 25%, and we have insourced over 40 new leakage specialists".
"We are working hard to build on the progress we're making, backed by record levels of investment across the region," the spokesperson said.
"We are transforming our network to improve long-term resilience of our water supply; protecting the environment and tackling leaks as part of our multibillion-pound plan to deliver the long-term improvements our customers and communities expect."
People were advised against bathing at Exmouth after a pollution incident last year [BBC]
A separate report from the Drinking Water Inspectorate, the Environment Agency, Natural Resources Wales and Ofwat said South West Water's drinking water quality "remains exceptional, and consumers can be confident that their water is safe to drink".
It noted although its internal sewer flooding performance had deteriorated, "it is still performing better than the industry average".
However, it said overall environmental performance "is poor".
In a summary, the report said overall water supply interruptions "remain a significant concern, and it is one of the worst performers in the industry".
To improve the company needed to reduce interruptions and complete a transformation programme to address the root causes of its failures and "substantially improve customer interactions and overall experience", it said.
Surfers Against Sewage described the latest performance ratings as "another league of shame for water companies" but she added they were "a mere slap on the wrist that means absolutely nothing".
Head of campaigns Jo Morley said: "What is the point in these environmental performance ratings when year after year water company behaviour gets worse?"

articles.title_orig: Mongolian mining company says copper exports have dropped due to China border restrictions - ABC News
articles.title_zh: Mongolian mining company says copper exports have dropped due to China border restrictions - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
The operator of one of Mongolia’s largest copper mines says its exports of copper concentrate to China have dropped by about 70% in the past two weeks due to restrictions at a border crossing
ULAANBAATAR, Mongolia -- The operator of one of Mongolia’s largest copper mines said Thursday its exports of copper concentrate to China have dropped by about 70% in the past two weeks due to restrictions at a border crossing.
The restrictions have raised concerns over potential revenue losses and disruptions to Mongolia’s massive mineral sector.
Oyu Tolgoi LLC, which operates Oyu Tolgoi, one of the world’s largest copper mines, said the number of truck convoys transporting copper concentrate across the Chinese border has fallen from the usual 12 to 13 per day to just around four. The restrictions affect vehicles crossing at China’s Ganqimaodu Border Port, which is adjacent to Mongolia’s Gashuunsukhait Border Port.
The export cuts amount to a decline of about $300 million compared to normal operating conditions and could reach $1.2 billion if restrictions continue through the end of the year, local media reported on Wednesday.
Oyu Tolgoi LLC did not confirm the reported losses in a statement to The Associated Press on Thursday.
Mongolia is a major supplier of coal and copper to China, the world’s largest consumer of both commodities.
Mongolian border officials said the slowdown was related to infrastructure and technology upgrades at China’s Ganqimaodu Border Port.
Authorities in China’s Inner Mongolia region did not immediately answer questions from the AP.
In August, Chinese authorities introduced an in-vehicle facial recognition system for truck drivers crossing the border, and installation and maintenance work have affected border processing capacity, according to the Mongolian border authorities.
Mongolia’s government said the Chinese embassy in Ulaanbaatar informed it that the work, originally due to end by late September according to Mongolian news reports, may continue until the end of December.
Mongolian Finance Minister Mendsaikhan Zagdjav said some ministers were instructed during a Cabinet meeting to visit the border crossing and meet with Chinese authorities, according to local news reports.
All transport routes on the Mongolian side remain open and the government was not aware of any political reasons behind the restrictions, said the minister of Road and Transport, Delgersaikhan Borkhuu.
Mongolia’s copper sector has become an increasingly important contributor to national export revenues. During the first nine months of 2026, copper concentrate exports reportedly reached 2 million tons.
The border crossing restrictions have also affected Mongolia’s coal exports through Gashuunsukhait, with the number of vehicles crossing falling to just over 1,000 a day from 1,300 a day, border authorities said.
Mongolia has abundant mineral resources, including coal, copper, gold, uranium and fluorspar, and its economy relies heavily on mining, which accounts for roughly a quarter of its GDP. It is particularly sensitive to disruptions to cross-border trade and fluctuations in commodity prices.
Last year, coal and copper concentrates together accounted for 82.3% of Mongolia’s merchandise exports, while 89.4% of total exports went to China. Mongolia was also China’s leading supplier of imported coking coal, accounting for approximately 51% of Chinese coking coal imports in 2025.

articles.title_orig: Why students in ancient China honoured teachers by gifting wild vegetables
articles.title_zh: Why students in ancient China honoured teachers by gifting wild vegetables
articles.content_orig:
Students gifted only water celery or white wormwood, choosing these fragrant plants to symbolise a pure pursuit of knowledge
While it is common for Chinese people to hold banquets for teachers upon graduation as a way of honouring them – a traditional value – in ancient China, students expressed their respect for teachers differently: by presenting them with vegetables.
The tradition began in the Zhou dynasty (1046–256 BC). On the first day of school, students wore blue gowns and brought their teachers wild vegetables they had gathered themselves. They then bowed reverently before memorial tablets honouring ancient sages. The ceremony was followed by a group dance, which also expressed the students’ respect for their teachers and their dedication to their studies.
Not just any vegetables could be presented to teachers on this day. Water celery and white wormwood were preferred because they were seen as clean, fragrant and ethereal, symbolising the students’ pure pursuit of knowledge.

articles.title_orig: An ‘Endless’ Cruise Around the World Is Suspended, Leaving Passengers Stranded
articles.title_zh: An ‘Endless’ Cruise Around the World Is Suspended, Leaving Passengers Stranded
articles.content_orig:
A US cruise ship MV. Odyssey docked at Sihanoukville Autonomous Port in Sihanoukville southern Cambodia, Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026. Heng Sinith/AP hide caption
SIHANOUKVILLE, Cambodia — A U.S. cruise ship on an around-the-world voyage that touted its cabins as floating homes suspended its three-year journey in Cambodia due to fuel costs, forcing hundreds of passengers to disembark.
The MV Odyssey set sail two years ago on a voyage to the seven continents marketed as combining long-term living at sea with global travel. Its operator had offered to "make the Odyssey your permanent home," with the purchase price of a suite for the lifetime of the vessel starting around $230,000.
For now, it is docked at the Cambodian port of Sihanoukville on the Gulf of Thailand, with no certain departure date.
The ship has been carrying 203 passengers, mostly Americans, along with 156 crew members, according to Cambodian officials. It has a 650-passenger capacity.
Its Florida-based operator, Villa Vie Residences, said monthly fuel expenses per cabin that historically averaged $1,800 have reached an estimated $6,000 to $8,000 in parts of Asia due to the war in Iran. The company said it sought to reduce fuel consumption by slowing the itinerary and spending more time in port, but was unable to offset the surging costs.
Traffic has been curtailed in the Strait of Hormuz since the war in Iran began, squeezing supplies of all kinds of petroleum-based fuels, especially in Southeast Asia, and sharply increasing prices.
"We have been unable to continue carrying the resulting operating losses," Villa Vie Residences said in a statement issued Tuesday. "Passing the full increase on to residents is not a realistic solution. Our focus now is on supporting residents, crew, and employees" while it tries to restructure.
"The company is working with residents to coordinate disembarkation and identify temporary living arrangements," it said.
Passengers, however, said they received no support and had to make their own arrangements after being given seven hours notice on Tuesday to disembark. Some were devastated and expressed hope a new company could rescue the venture so life at sea can continue.
Paul and Lynn Montoya, a retired couple from Wyoming, said they bought a window cabin and had expected to sail for years. They boarded the ship 17 months ago in Panama.
A couple passenger from a U.S. cruise ship, the MV Odyssey, Paul Montoya, left, stands for an interview with his wife, Lynn Motoya, at the Independence Hotel in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. Heng Sinith/AP hide caption
Paul praised the concept of residential cruising but said the shipowner lacked the expertise to make the business financially sustainable. While rising fuel costs had been cited publicly as the reason for the suspension, he said the company had already been struggling. Changes to itinerary, unreliable internet access and declining food quality had pushed many residents to leave the ship in recent months, he said.
Lynn said residents were repeatedly asked to contribute additional money for fuel and other expenses, including a fresh call to raise funds for fuel to get out of Cambodia. She said the crew members were also not paid.
"We were tired of every two to four weeks being asked for money for fuel, money for everything," she said. "We had hopes but they just kept sinking further and further into the hole through mismanagement."
The company could not immediately be contacted for comment.
Yet for some, even the financial and logistical turmoil couldn't outweigh the extraordinary experience of traveling the world and living at sea.
Carol Larson, 69, and her sister Crystal Lavering, 72, occupied separate cabins aboard the ship for 18 months. The siblings, from California, described the suspension as heartbreaking, and hoped the cruise would be resuscitated.
A sibling passenger from a U.S. cruise ship, the MV Odyssey, Carol Larson, 69, left, stands for an interview with her sister, Crystal Lavering, at the Independence Hotel in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. Heng Sinith/AP hide caption
"I hope there is a movement for the residents to buy the ship and I am hoping that goes through because it's a dream to live on the ship and I don't want it to end," Larson said.
Lavering said her health improved during her time on the ship, and that she didn't need to use a cane to walk anymore. "You come to this ship to live … it's just sad that it's all over."
Larson bought her cabin for $120,000, paid in installments, in addition to monthly maintenance fees, under a plan that had promised the possibility of living aboard for up to 15 years. She said she blamed U.S. President Donald Trump for the ship's woes as fuel costs spiked due to the Iran war, in addition to poor management. But she said she didn't regret her investment.
"Because it was a startup company, I believe that it was a risk. From the very first day, I said to myself that if it lasts a year, I can walk away and feel like I got my money's worth … I still feel that way. I feel blessed to have been part of the experiment of residential cruising," she said.
The ship arrived in Sihanoukville last Friday and was scheduled to depart Wednesday, according to a statement from Long Dimanche, the deputy governor of Preah Sihanouk province. He said it was now expected to refuel and depart Cambodia on Saturday, but the ship's operator has not yet publicly confirmed any date.
A U.S. cruise ship, the MV Odyssey, docks at the Sihanoukville Autonomous Port in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, late Wednesday evening, Oct. 28, 2026. Heng Sinith/AP hide caption
Built in 1993 and operated under different names by several cruise lines over the years before being becalmed by the coronavirus pandemic in 2020, the Odyssey was bought by Villa Vie Residences in 2023.
Its current cruise, originally intended to last 3 1/2 years, began in October 2024 in Belfast, Northern Ireland, where the ship had been refitted. A second cruise had been tentatively scheduled to end in August 2030.
The Odyssey is not the first cruise ship Sihanoukville has hosted in crisis.
In February 2020, the MS Westerdam was allowed to dock in Cambodia after being turned away at five ports in other nations because of fears of COVID-19, which just a month earlier had started to spread from China. It carried 1,455 passengers, more than 600 of them American citizens.
After being stranded at sea for two weeks, Cambodia's then-Prime Minister Hun Sen allowed it to dock for what he said were humanitarian reasons. Cambodia won plaudits as passengers were welcomed ashore and arrangements were made for them to fly home.

articles.title_orig: SpaceX stock slides back toward $140 as smaller space names leave it behind
articles.title_zh: SpaceX stock slides back toward $140 as smaller space names leave it behind
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
SpaceX took its worst one-day hit last Thursday since early August, when its biggest share unlock yet freed up to 1.3 billion shares to trade. Roughly a week later, it's back at the same floor, and the rest of the space trade has left it behind.
SpaceX ( SPCX ) shares slipped again on Thursday during premarket trading, along with nearly every space stock.
$140 has been SpaceX's floor since the summer. It marked the top of the stock's August trading range before a breakout, and it sits about halfway between the August low near $108 and the $172 ceiling that capped rallies in June and October.
That makes $140 support , a price where buyers have repeatedly stepped in. They did it twice this month, and the stock is back there again.
SpaceX fell about 9% on Oct. 22 as those shares unlocked.
Since then, the smaller names have done the running. Rocket Lab ( RKLB ), Firefly Aerospace ( FLY ), Intuitive Machines ( LUNR ) and AST SpaceMobile ( ASTS ) gained roughly 8% to 14% from the Oct. 22 close through Tuesday, while SpaceX barely budged.
That bounce followed a much rougher month for the group: over the past 30 days, those four are down roughly 20% to 35%, compared with a loss of about 3% for SpaceX.
The pullback comes as investors gear up for Anthropic's IPO, the next mega-listing, with JPMorgan again set to lead retail share sales as it did for SpaceX. SpaceX sits about a third below its June record close near $212.
A sustained break below $140 would open the door to a deeper slide toward the August low near $108. To turn the chart around, bulls first need to get back above the 50-day moving average, near $150, before taking another run at $172.
Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Alphabet ( GOOGL ) report after the bell. How much more they plan to spend building AI data centers is the number most likely to move a stock that's now mostly an AI company .

In an official statement released on its Japanese website on Thursday, the company acknowledged that the Japanese spy drama contained content that “does not align with the Sanrio Group’s corporate philosophy”.
The controversial series includes scenes depicting Chinese intelligence agents torturing Japanese operatives, prompting China’s state broadcaster CCTV to accuse the show of distorting history and “deliberately smearing” Beijing.
In its statement, Sanrio confirmed that it was ceasing the current collaboration with Vivant – which premiered in 2023 and opened its second season in July – along with all related future projects and promotional campaigns.
